# Public workflow simulator fixtures

These sanitized JSON files are internal test inputs for Client Workflow Rehearsal. They are not activated workflows and may be used only through the in-process synthetic service simulator. The files retain third-party workflow structure under the attribution below; they are not part of any public demo/export bundle.

n8n's self-serve terms say public Community Materials may be used and adapted by other users in their own projects. The public workflow directory appears to fit that category, but this is an inference. Keep the fixtures internal, keep these source links and author names, and do not republish the exports. Source terms read 2026-11-10: <https://n8n.io/legal/self-serve-terms/>.

## Sanitization

- The source API envelopes were flattened to the exported workflow object. Workflow IDs, versions, timestamps, tags, meta, pinned/static execution data and webhook IDs were removed; all fixtures are inactive.
- Sticky-note annotation nodes were removed. One 10-digit phone-shaped value occurred in a sticky note in workflow 8258; the note is absent from the fixture and the raw source was not retained in the repository. The embedded GitHub owner/repository and Notion database ID in 1804 were replaced with synthetic values; the shared webhook path in 8258 was replaced with `synthetic-contacts`.
- Credential references in workflows 1804, 16081, 8258, 14745, 2713 and 5889 were replaced with type-only source markers. No credential values were present in the inspected exports. Workflow 20047 retains credential-type markers; the n8n resource owner now maps the pinned LangChain OpenAI chat/embedding and Pinecone vector node types to synthetic credentials. Runtime credential resolution remains unverified.
- Workflow 20047's `your-store.com` site host and Pinecone console-host placeholder were rewritten to `wordpress.synthetic.invalid` and `pinecone.synthetic.invalid`; workflow 22567 had its program-generated URL replaced with a fixed `api.synthetic.invalid` route, account placeholders replaced by synthetic literals, query/header auth disabled, and node notes removed. URL query strings and fragments were stripped from literal URL fields. Dynamic URL expressions remain data and are interpreted only by the simulator.
- Workflow 2713's `api.firecrawl.dev` endpoint was replaced by a fixed `crawl.synthetic.invalid` route. The HTTP Header Auth reference, header fields and expression body were omitted from the sanitized fixture; the caller URL is not interpreted or forwarded. A synthetic caller workflow was added solely to invoke the actual public subworkflow through the existing generic Execute Workflow adapter.
- Workflow 8995's seven sticky notes were removed; its lead-specific OpenAI prompt, model selector, sheet/document references, recipient, message, subject, and Slack destination were replaced with synthetic data. The export has no credential objects. Its three main output-port links from the legacy OpenAI node are not modeled as ordinary success fan-out, so its import test rejects the graph instead of guessing which links should run.
- Workflow 6920's two sticky notes were removed; recipient and message content were replaced with synthetic values. It was run as the error-handler child in a generic synthetic bundle whose primary HTTP request fails on an unmapped synthetic route. This verifies the simulator's configured error-workflow routing and the sanitized public child graph; it does not prove n8n runtime Error Trigger behavior.
- Workflow 21098's three sticky notes were removed; webhook path, sheet/document/channel identifiers, response text, lead content, recipient and outbound message were replaced with synthetic values. The 328-byte Code source was retained as inert attributed data and interpreted only by the bounded Go subset. Its single Filter condition, webhook, Sheets append, Slack post, Gmail send and webhook response were preserved. Source export and page-data API nodes/connections/settings have identical canonical graph data; only sanitized fixture data is retained.
- Workflow 16079's top-level template metadata, workflow UUID/version/meta, pinned/static data, webhook ID and four sticky-note nodes were excluded; only its canonical `workflow` graph is retained. The HTTP Request host is `openai.synthetic.invalid`, static header/auth fields were removed, email values are synthetic `.invalid`, and the Sheets `documentId` is `synthetic-sheet-document`. The 19-node/20-edge graph and four Code bodies were retained as inert public source. A secret-token-pattern scan is clean; the 15 email-shaped strings are synthetic. Code and Set expressions now parse in the shared bounded Go evaluator, including optional properties, computed lookups, `let` assignment, `parseInt`, `split` and named prior-node context. Import still fails closed because `Slack — Duplicate Warning` declares `resource=chat`, invalid for the pinned Slack V2.3 node (its resource default is `message`, and `chat` is not an option). Test `TestPublic16079RejectedBecauseItsPinnedSlackResourceIsInvalid` preserves this evidence. The export is not rewritten or bypassed and does not count as a run.
- Static review of Code/Function nodes found only data transformations, batching and delay selection; none contained direct network, process or file calls. No email addresses or common credential-token patterns were found in sanitized files.
- Service nodes still describe external effects (GitHub/Notion, Postgres, Supabase, WordPress, OpenAI and Pinecone). No real service calls have occurred. The simulator must replace those effects with synthetic state and documented/recorded service behavior; these files are not safe to run directly against external APIs.

Workflow 8011 was fetched from the official template API (51,071 B, SHA-256 `6b9e4b8be6ff9b5cc6611444813d5f99e721607d3b218eb1aca4d60f0b85b809`), author cong-nguyen, [source page](https://n8n.io/workflows/8011-conversational-sales-agent-for-woocommerce-with-gpt-4-stripe-and-crm-integration/). The sanitized fixture `8011.json` (`43f7814e7d9a0181002b335cffdbb17162f2935d1fa6b97269efe76436591ffb`) retains the 24 non-note source nodes and 22 source connections, while removing metadata/pinned data, credential objects and webhook IDs, replacing the chat destination, external child-workflow references and Qdrant URL with synthetic values, and removing HTTP auth/header/body fields. Static scans found no email or common token matches; phone-like regex matches were UUID-shaped node identifiers. It is retained without import/run or score credit: LangChain node families, AI connection edges, and external child-workflow semantics are not modeled.

Public workflow 5333 retains the 7-node executable graph after dropping its one sticky note. Both omitted Google Sheets operations resolve to `sheet.read` only for pinned Google Sheets V2 node version 4.6; its two synthetic feed collections are selected by generic `sheetName` input match. RSS Feed Read accepts only a bounded HTTPS `*.synthetic.invalid` URL and invokes an exact synthetic profile; no feed is fetched. The source Code body is interpreted by the bounded read-only named-node context to exclude previously posted links. Synthetic Sheets append and Slack post are recorded against fixed profile fixtures. Fixture hash `aaf6901ee404de4f1d8a3caa75504a1ee7a9a45afed29d9ee271f1215751522e`; this is in-process generic simulator evidence, not native n8n execution or durable handoff.

Original API export bytes and hashes are recorded above for provenance. Sanitized fixture hashes and exact node/edge counts are in the F7 run's `PUBLIC-WORKFLOW-SAMPLE.md`. Fixture 8258 is now imported and synthetically run by the client-rehearsal API test `TestPublicSupabaseWorkflowRunsSelectedWebhookBranchesInSyntheticSimulator` on four webhook paths (GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE). It produces an in-memory handoff awaiting human review; the run is test evidence, not persisted showcase evidence. The Supabase route responses are fixed OpenAPI examples, not stateful CRUD. The digest-pinned n8n image has since been acquired under host disk admission, but no n8n runtime or third-party service was used. Fixture 1804 remains unimported/unrun and has no repair or delivery credit. Fixture 20047 now imports and runs through both its manual and schedule paths in `TestPublic20047ImportsLangChainAIDataflow`, using generic typed AI attachments and synthetic WordPress, Data Table, and Pinecone API descriptions. Embeddings are deterministic hash projections, not OpenAI model output; Pinecone and Data Table responses are fixed profile examples, with no stateful persistence, durable handoff, n8n runtime or repair credit. Fixture 14745 is now imported and synthetically run through the generic bounded Code/loop/Wait engine on both its manual and schedule triggers, with 25 synthetic Supabase writes per trigger; this adds one distinct public run but no durable handoff, n8n runtime, or repair credit. The 8995 graph is excluded after pinned node-source inspection; 6920 is synthetically exercised through generic configured error routing, with no n8n runtime or live mail.

Workflow 22567 is now imported and synthetically executed through the generic OpenAPI catalog, bounded manual Set assignments and Split Out branches; its URL program is not executed. Its invoice/payment examples are fixed synthetic outcomes. A seeded missing-array selector was detected in failed run `9035f8bf-46d2-4e86-897d-91d12d74777e`; corrected public revision `71c2bf3d-ba6f-46de-bfa5-60d93edb938c` reached `needs_review` with repair lineage. See `repairs/22567/REPAIR.md`. This is generic simulator evidence only, not actual n8n runtime, SQL/HTTP execution, or stateful service behavior.

Workflow 2713 is imported as a child in a synthetic parent bundle and executed through the generic OpenAPI description catalog. The public child uses its subworkflow trigger, one HTTP Request and a Set projection; the credential was replaced, the destination is `.invalid`, and its source request body is discarded. The Set adapter accepts only literal values or bounded `$json` path projections; arbitrary expressions remain rejected. The running Client Workflow Rehearsal service also created and returned the durable handoff, then the owning CLI re-read it as `b2736ade-d928-4bd8-a00c-d9161ba7e1aa` with state `needs_review`. The service was stopped after that check. No n8n runtime or public crawl occurred and no seeded-defect repair is claimed.

Workflow 16081 repair lineage: seeded Switch selector mutation and durable failed/corrected runs are detailed in the F7 run folder `repairs/16081/REPAIR.md`. The corrected unchanged public revision executes only a synthetic predeclared Postgres SELECT response; no SQL runs. Workflow 21013 repair lineage: the seeded omission of `valid` and durable failed/corrected runs are detailed in `repairs/21013/REPAIR.md`; the corrected persisted run safely follows the invalid-form response branch without Gmail or Sheets effects. Both repairs are distinct workflows and both handoffs remain `needs_review`.


16364 fixture SHA-256 `19217657f3142431844d90963efe9354ecac7d4eace685f4c7827ac5164cc295` passes the in-process generic simulator from its Schedule trigger. It reads two generic Sheets routes selected by input `sheetName`, filters the deterministic 2026-11-11 row, builds HTML and simulates two Gmail sends to `.invalid` recipients. Durable seeded wrong-tab failure `6d1c1846-79e3-4239-8202-b0ccd5d81ac4` and corrected `needs_review` handoff `fd9b4d8c-64f0-4a66-97b1-db0be5a447a5` were both read back through the scenario CLI. No n8n runtime or real account was used.

Workflow 1804 sanitized fixture SHA-256 `f07ea4384b83db37b3f999bdfce143c83e477ebd3defff2e8f0f02a8eb377ce8` runs unchanged from its GitHub polling trigger against generic synthetic Notion outcomes for opened, edited, deleted, closed and reopened actions. Durable seeded wrong-return-shape failure `d2ddeec9-7fd6-4997-958d-e19a4770a070` and corrected `needs_review` handoff `f29b42c9-3619-4802-b5cc-8fec2dc70cbf` were read back through the scenario CLI. The simulator remains stateless and no native runtime or real account was used.


Public workflow 20819 — “Log workflow failures to Google Sheets and alert on Telegram,” by Mashrur Rahman ([source](https://n8n.io/workflows/20819-log-workflow-failures-to-google-sheets-and-send-telegram-alerts/)); official API export 32,114 bytes, SHA-256 `a66769878f45aa36ce9dbe42b4989de32e0a36d8c78c9fddda415366ed6f3c5f`. Sanitized fixture SHA-256 `53973d7f35333414bce805f680460c0c073e3942a6a675368d3429434eb7ad33`. Seven executable nodes and six edges; five sticky notes removed. Credential destinations and identifying workflow metadata were replaced or omitted. Static review found no direct network, process or file calls in the Code nodes. The generic simulator test binds the unchanged public graph as the configured error child of a synthetic parent whose operation fails; it executes the Error Trigger, Set, per-item bounded Code, synthetic Sheets append and Telegram send. A second run omits the Sheets operation from the declared generic profile and verifies the exported `continueErrorOutput` branch emits its separate synthetic Telegram outage alert. The simulator profile is inert and no real message/service effect occurred. No seeded repair or native n8n claim.

## Workflow 16667 — Notify on server restarts via Discord, Telegram and Slack

- Author: Kris Hoang. [Official template page](https://n8n.io/workflows/16667-notify-on-server-restarts-with-discord-telegram-and-slack-alerts/).
- Official API source export: 47,539 bytes; SHA-256 `c82e60548f4d80739b79cd6c932879b0a64c315685f3e5acdcd9047b5b0d5a4d`.
- Sanitized internal candidate: `16667.json`, 13,177 bytes; SHA-256 `f2b0b6c5c2b1ba9bac9d943ab7b5aeb9b67655b87733bcab2c29c6a35289605a`.
- The candidate retains the 11 executable nodes and 11 main edges, including the n8n instance restart trigger, n8n execution-log query, filter/summarize/sort/merge/code path and Discord, Telegram and Slack nodes. Six sticky notes and workflow/template identity metadata were removed. Credential objects and destination identifiers were omitted or replaced; alert text is synthetic and the fallback host became `n8n.synthetic.invalid`. The 4,179-byte Code body was scanned for direct network, process and file calls; none were found. Sanitized fixture scans found no email-shaped or secret-shaped values. It has not been imported or run; the generic engine does not yet prove all node families, n8n instance-event semantics or notification outcomes. No simulator-run credit or message delivery is claimed. The raw export was removed after provenance capture.
